html:
Avanti was one of the sixteen great kingdoms of ancient India, the Mahajanapadas, in the Malwa region of central India. Its main city was Ujjain.

In the time of the Buddha, around the 5th century BCE, its king Pradyota was one of the four strongest rulers of north India, a rival of Magadha. Buddhist and Jain stories call him fierce. Ujjain sat on trade routes from the Ganges plain to the ports of the western coast, which made Avanti rich.

Magadha absorbed Avanti around the 4th century BCE. Under the Maurya Empire Ujjain was a provincial capital, and the young Ashoka served there as governor before he became emperor.
sum: Avanti was one of the sixteen great kingdoms of ancient India, the Mahajanapadas, in the Malwa region of central India. Its main city was Ujjain.
